section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Reynolds Number (Re)
section_1.content: Define turbulence as a transition from laminar flow. Introduce the Reynolds Number (Re = ρvL/μ) as the dimensionless ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. Use a visual 'speed gauge' animation transitioning from smooth fluid layers to chaotic vortices as Re increases.
section_1.example: A toy submarine moving through a pool: slow motion (low Re) shows smooth flow lines; rapid acceleration (high Re) triggers wake vortices.

section_2.title: The Kolmogorov Cascade & Universal Constants
section_2.content: Explain energy transfer from large-scale eddies to small-scale dissipation via the 'Richardson Cascade.' Introduce the Kolmogorov constant (C ≈ 1.5) as the universal scaling factor that links energy dissipation rate (ε) to the spectrum of turbulence.
section_2.example: A whirlpool in a bathtub: the large swirling vortex breaking down into smaller, spinning foam-bubbles until they vanish into microscopic heat.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Structure: The -5/3 Power Law
section_3.content: Present the Kolmogorov -5/3 spectrum. Graphically demonstrate a log-log plot of Energy Density (E) vs. Wave Number (k). Show how the slope of -5/3 emerges in the 'inertial range,' representing the self-similar structure of eddies.
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'fractal' tree: each branch splits into smaller branches following a self-similar ratio, just as large eddies break into geometrically similar smaller eddies.

section_4.title: Application: Why Constant Matters
section_4.content: Summarize how these mathematical constants allow us to predict high-speed turbulence (which is otherwise uncomputable) by modeling the universal inertial range. Emphasize that these constants hold true regardless of the fluid (air vs. water).
section_4.example: An aerospace engineer using the -5/3 power law to predict drag forces on a jet engine's turbine blade, allowing the engine to run without melting.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Why Constant Matters", [
            "Constants predict uncomputable high-speed flows.",
            "Model universal inertial range simply.",
            "Constants hold across diverse fluids."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        flow_visual = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(flow_visual, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        eqn = MathTex(r"E(k) = C \epsilon^{2/3} k^{-5/3}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eqn, 'E4', scale_factor=1.2)
